ui.meta.title: Staša Čimbur — hats, headpieces and textile collages
ui.meta.description: Staša Čimbur (StashaHats), applied artist and master milliner between Zagreb and Amsterdam: hats, fascinators, bags, parasols, scarves and sewn textile collages.
ui.a11y.floorPlan: Floor plan of the salon: jump to a room
ui.prolog.title: Prologue
ui.prolog.p1: Staša Čimbur sews small performances for the head, the hands and the wall. Hats, fascinators, bags, parasols, scarves and printed fabrics come out of her studios in Zagreb and Amsterdam, and the material always leads: a scrap of old velvet, lace from a flea market, a felt that refuses to bend.
ui.prolog.p2: She has more than 150 exhibitions, performances and shows behind her, among them the solo exhibition “All you need is a Hat” at the Museum of Arts and Crafts in Zagreb. Her work is held in museums and private collections, and she has collaborated with Josipa Lisac on stage and off.
ui.prolog.portraitAlt: Portrait of Staša Čimbur wearing one of her hats
ui.wing1.title: Wearable
ui.wing1.intro: Six rooms, one walk. Keep scrolling and the salon moves with you.
ui.interlude.quote: A hat is not decoration. A hat is {eye} an entrance onto the stage.
ui.wing2.title: For the wall
ui.wing2.intro: Sewn textile collages and objects, framed and ready for your wall. Each one exists only once.
ui.exh.title: Exhibitions and press
ui.exh.name: Title
ui.comm.title: Commissions
ui.comm.p: A bespoke hat starts with a conversation: about the occasion, about the head, and about how much courage you would like to wear. Making one takes three to eight weeks. I also make costume pieces for the stage, one-off pieces for weddings, and work for exhibitions.

pl-001.title: Theatre Box
pl-001.story: A wide brim of black felt and a veil scattered with red dots: a hat that watches from the balcony. Worn to a premiere at the Croatian National Theatre, where it reportedly drew more glances than the stage.
pl-001.alt: Hat of felt, tulle and velvet, in red, white and black

pl-002.title: Sunday Bolero
pl-002.story: A cloche in poppy-red felt with an appliquéd satin band that turns around the head like a dance step. Made for a walk that lasts all afternoon.
pl-002.alt: Hat of felt and satin, in red, white and black

pl-003.title: Confetti Rain
pl-003.story: A straw hat with hand-sewn sequins falling down the brim as if the party has only just ended. First shown at a runway show in Amsterdam.
pl-003.alt: Hat of straw, sequins and thread, in red, white and black

pl-004.title: Madam Three-Eyes
pl-004.story: A black velvet pillbox with three embroidered eyes that seem to blink when the wearer turns her head. A hat that notices everything you miss.
pl-004.alt: Hat of velvet, silk and thread, in red, white and black

pl-005.title: A Drop of Red
pl-005.story: A teardrop fascinator blocked from red sinamay and a single feather. Small enough for the office, bold enough for a wedding.
pl-005.alt: Headpiece of sinamay and feathers, in red, white and black

pl-006.title: Swallowtail
pl-006.story: Two wings of black felt on a fine wire, edged in white silk. When the wind picks up, the headpiece sways as if it might fly away.
pl-006.alt: Headpiece of felt, wire and silk, in red, white and black

pl-007.title: Whisper Behind the Veil
pl-007.story: A small satin cap with a tulle veil and old lace found at the Hrelić flea market. The veil covers one eye and leaves the other free to wink.
pl-007.alt: Headpiece of tulle, lace and satin, in red, white and black

pl-008.title: Small Crown for a Big Day
pl-008.story: A crown of red felt with brass studs and sequins, worn slightly askew. For birthdays, resignations and other big decisions.
pl-008.alt: Headpiece of brass, felt and sequins, in red, white and black

pl-009.title: The Unsent Letter
pl-009.story: An envelope clutch with a red leather seal and a polka-dot cotton lining. Inside there is room for a lipstick, a key and one sentence you never said.
pl-009.alt: Bag of leather, cotton and thread, in red, white and black

pl-010.title: Polka for Leaving
pl-010.story: A printed cotton bag with wooden handles, big enough for a weekend out of town. The dots are printed by hand, so no two are quite alike.
pl-010.alt: Bag of cotton, wood and leather, in red, white and black

pl-011.title: Pocket for Secrets
pl-011.story: A small velvet pouch with a brass clasp and an eye embroidered on the flap. The eye stays awake even when the bag is shut.
pl-011.alt: Bag of velvet, brass and silk, in red, white and black

pl-012.title: Little Dance Box
pl-012.story: A box-shaped bag with a pleated satin flounce around its base. When you walk, the flounce swings like a skirt on the dance floor.
pl-012.alt: Bag of leather, satin and lace, in red, white and black

pl-013.title: Shade for Flamenco
pl-013.story: A parasol of striped cotton with a lace edge and a wooden handle. The hem is cut into waves, like the lowest tier of a flamenco skirt.
pl-013.alt: Parasol of cotton, lace and wood, in red, white and black

pl-014.title: Polka-dot Sky
pl-014.story: A silk parasol printed with white dots on black, so that it is always night underneath. The brass tip follows an old Viennese pattern.
pl-014.alt: Parasol of silk, wood and brass, in red, white and black

pl-015.title: Sunshade for Amsterdam Rain
pl-015.story: A sunshade that keeps hoping for sun, even in November. The raindrops embroidered on the inside can only be seen by whoever is carrying it.
pl-015.alt: Parasol of cotton, wood and thread, in red, white and black

pl-016.title: Turning Circle
pl-016.story: A pleated parasol of paper and silk that opens like a fan. Made for a performance in which twenty parasols turned to the same rhythm.
pl-016.alt: Parasol of paper, wood and silk, in red, white and black

pl-018.title: Hands on the Wall
pl-018.story: A silk scarf printed with hands, eyes and little faces drawn in ink in vertical bands. The same drawing later became the wallpaper of her studio.
pl-018.alt: Scarf of silk, in red, white and black

pl-019.title: Lashes
pl-019.story: A long scarf with a repeat of red eyes with long lashes. Wrapped around the neck, the eyes look in every direction at once.
pl-019.alt: Scarf of cotton and silk, in red, white and black

pl-020.title: Stripes for the Sea
pl-020.story: A linen tablecloth, or a cape, depending on the wind: red and white stripes with a hand-rolled hem. Made on the island of Vis during one very long summer.
pl-020.alt: Scarf of linen and cotton, in red, white and black

pl-021.title: Little Circus
pl-021.story: A scarf on which acrobats, horses and one puzzled lion circle a red centre. The edges are embroidered in red thread, stitch by stitch.
pl-021.alt: Scarf of silk and thread, in red, white and black

pl-022.title: Flounce for Midnight
pl-022.story: A skirt in four tiers of flounces — red, polka-dot, white and lace — like the collage that inspired it. Made for dancing that starts after midnight.
pl-022.alt: Garment of satin, tulle and lace, in red, white and black

pl-023.title: Coat with Eyes
pl-023.story: A black felt coat with appliquéd eyes on the back, so the wearer always knows who is walking behind her. Each eye has a different expression.
pl-023.alt: Garment of felt, cotton and thread, in red, white and black

pl-024.title: Lace Bolero
pl-024.story: A short bolero pieced together from seven different antique laces and a single red button. Every lace has its own story and its own grandmother.
pl-024.alt: Garment of lace, silk and buttons, in red, white and black

pl-025.title: Dress for Making an Entrance
pl-025.story: A dress with a striped bodice and a tulle skirt that rustles when the wearer enters a room. Leaving, according to the maker, matters less.
pl-025.alt: Garment of cotton, satin and tulle, in red, white and black

pl-017.title: Matador's Darling
pl-017.story: A dancer in tiers of flamenco flounces rushes diagonally across the stage, in front of a wallpaper of hands and eyes. Red eyes blink on her stockings: the work this whole salon grew from.
pl-017.alt: Framed textile collage of cotton, lace, silk and thread, in red, white and black

pl-026.title: Dancer on a Wire
pl-026.story: A small dancer balances on a real wire sewn across a polka-dot ground. There is no net below her, only the black floor.
pl-026.alt: Framed textile collage of cotton, wire and thread, in red, white and black

pl-027.title: Salon of Hands
pl-027.story: Twelve hands cut from printed fabric greet, point and wave. One of them holds a hat that nobody is wearing.
pl-027.alt: Framed textile collage of cotton, paper and thread, in red, white and black

pl-028.title: Red Curtain
pl-028.story: A velvet curtain is just parting, and behind it all you can see is one leg in a polka-dot stocking. The rest of the show you have to imagine.
pl-028.alt: Framed textile collage of velvet, satin and thread, in red, white and black

pl-029.title: Portrait of a Lady in a Hat
pl-029.story: Her face is white silk and her hat three layers of lace that spill over the frame. The lady looks straight at you and does not blink.
pl-029.alt: Framed textile collage of silk, lace and buttons, in red, white and black

pl-030.title: The Cat Who Saw Everything
pl-030.story: A black felt cat sits at a window, and her red eyes follow anyone who crosses the room. The smallest work on the wall, and the most reliable guard.
pl-030.alt: Framed textile collage of felt, cotton and thread, in red, white and black

pl-031.title: Night Train Zagreb – Amsterdam
pl-031.story: A long horizontal collage of carriage windows, a different hat in each one. The seam that joins them is the railway, embroidered in red thread along its whole length.
pl-031.alt: Framed textile collage of cotton, linen and thread, in red, white and black

pl-032.title: Cabaret on the Balcony
pl-032.story: Three singers on a balcony of lace, each keeping her own time. The sequins are sewn on one by one, like notes.
pl-032.alt: Framed textile collage of satin, sequins and lace, in red, white and black

pl-033.title: Love Letter to a Milliner
pl-033.story: A hat that cannot be worn: a sculpture of felt, wire and old hat blocks from her studio. A dedication to every milliner who taught her.
pl-033.alt: Wearable object of felt, wire, paper and thread, in red, white and black

pl-034.title: Eye in a Shoe
pl-034.story: An old dancing shoe in which an embroidered eye lives instead of a foot. An object for a vitrine, not for dancing, although nobody believes that.
pl-034.alt: Wearable object of leather, silk and thread, in red, white and black

pl-035.title: Three Sisters, One Hat
pl-035.story: Three sisters share one large red hat, and none of them wants to let go. A collage about family inheritance and about who is next in line.
pl-035.alt: Wearable object of felt, cotton and lace, in red, white and black

pl-036.title: Rose and Polka
pl-036.story: A large red silk rose climbs out of a polka-dot hat as if from a theatre box. A sculpture that can hang on a wall or, with a little courage, be worn.
pl-036.alt: Wearable object of silk, felt and wire, in red, white and black
